title: Realtime client links dropped
description: 20 SSE and 20 WebSocket clients on one topic through a TCP proxy, 50 messages per second published by a function; every client link cut for 1 s (inside the 100-event replay buffer), then for 4 s (past it), the node and its hub running throughout
result: 745 messages published (745×200); SSE missed 0–0 of 50 inside the buffer and 105–109 of 200 past it; every client reconnected 2–2 times; meter 371.9 s vs 368.7 s measured
target: one reconnect per drop; SSE contiguous inside the replay buffer; past it, the buffer's events only and no error; no RENOX_REALTIME_LIMIT; meter seconds = connection seconds (±5 %)

checks.name: each cut drops every client link
each client reconnects exactly once per cut
checks.detail: reconnects per client: min 2, max 2 (2 cuts)

checks.name: SSE inside the replay buffer: nothing missed
checks.detail: 50 events published during the 1 s cut; missing across the reconnect per client 0–0; every connection's stream without hole or repeat: true

checks.name: SSE past the buffer: the newest 100 replayed, the older ones gone
checks.detail: 200 events during the 4 s cut; missing across the reconnect per client 105–109 (expected 100, plus what was published before the client was back)

checks.name: WebSocket: no replay, a clean stream after each reconnect
checks.detail: missing across the reconnects per client 53–54 of 50 and 208–209 of 200 published during the cuts; every connection's stream without hole or repeat: true

checks.name: the meter records sum to the connection seconds
checks.detail: 120 records (60 WS, 60 SSE) for 120 connections; realtime_conn_seconds 371.9 s, client-measured 368.7 s (0.9 %)

notes: The replay buffer is 100 events or 60 s, whichever is shorter (ops.md section 18): at 50 messages per second it holds 2 s, so the long cut is past it although it is well under 60 s.
Past the buffer no event names the gap (#281 implements none; the contract says the client re-reads its state); the SSE `id:` jumps.

The clients close while messages are still published: on a quiet topic the node sees an SSE client leave only at its next 15 s keep-alive (ops.md section 18), so that connection is metered until then.
The cut is of the client links only; a worker restart takes the hub and its buffer with it (ids restart at 1), which no scenario here asserts.
